question: A post office requires different numbers of full-time employees on different days of the week. The number of full-time employees required on each day is given in Table 4. Monday requires 17 employees,Tuesday requires13, Wednesday requires 15, Thursday requires 19, Friday requires 14, Saturday requires 16,  Sunday requires 11. Union rules state that each full-time employee must work five consecutive days and then receive two days off. For example, an employee who works Monday to Friday must be off on Saturday and Sunday. The post office wants to meet its daily requirements using only fulltime employees. Formulate an LP that the post office can use to minimize the number of full-time employees who must be hired. Find the minimal number.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# All numeric constants from the problem statement
DATA = {
    "days": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"],
    "requirements": {
        "Mon": 17,  # "Monday requires 17 employees"
        "Tue": 13,  # "Tuesday requires13"
        "Wed": 15,  # "Wednesday requires 15"
        "Thu": 19,  # "Thursday requires 19"
        "Fri": 14,  # "Friday requires 14"
        "Sat": 16,  # "Saturday requires 16"
        "Sun": 11,  # "Sunday requires 11"
    },
    "work_days": 5,  # "each full-time employee must work five consecutive days"
    "off_days": 2,   # "and then receive two days off"
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    days = d["days"]
    n = len(days)
    work = d["work_days"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Shift-start variables: x[s] = employees whose 5-day block starts on day s.
    # assumption: shift_pattern_orientation x[s] covers s, s+1, ..., s+4 (cyclic week)
    # "each full-time employee must work five consecutive days and then receive two days off"
    model.S = pyo.Set(initialize=days)
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.S,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,  # assumption: variable_domain NonNegativeReals
    )

    # Objective: minimize total employees hired = sum of all shift-start variables.
    # "minimize the number of full-time employees who must be hired"
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[s] for s in m.S)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Coverage constraints: each day must be covered by at least its requirement.
    # "The post office wants to meet its daily requirements"
    # assumption: coverage_constraint_direction >= requirement
    # assumption: cyclic_week_wrap (block starting Saturday covers Sat,Sun,Mon,Tue,Wed)
    def cover_rule(m, day):
        idx = days.index(day)
        # employees working on `day` are those whose block start is within the
        # previous (work-1) days through `day` itself, cyclically
        starts = [days[(idx - k) % n] for k in range(work)]
        return sum(m.x[s] for s in starts) >= d["requirements"][day]

    model.cover = pyo.Constraint(model.S, rule=cover_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# All numeric constants from the problem statement.
DATA = {
    "days": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"],
    # "Monday requires 17 employees,Tuesday requires13, Wednesday requires 15,
    #  Thursday requires 19, Friday requires 14, Saturday requires 16, Sunday requires 11."
    "requirements": {
        "Mon": 17,
        "Tue": 13,
        "Wed": 15,
        "Thu": 19,
        "Fri": 14,
        "Sat": 16,
        "Sun": 11,
    },
    # "each full-time employee must work five consecutive days and then receive two days off"
    "work_days": 5,
    "off_days": 2,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    days = d["days"]
    req = d["requirements"]
    n = len(days)

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # x[s] = employees whose 2-day off block starts on day s (covers all days except s, s+1)
    # assumption: shift_pattern_orientation per modelling decisions
    model.S = pyo.Set(initialize=days)
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.S,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        # "minimize the number of full-time employees who must be hired"
        bounds=(0, None),
    )

    # Objective: minimize total employees hired = sum of all shift-start variables
    # "minimize the number of full-time employees who must be hired"
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[s] for s in m.S)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Coverage: each day must be covered by at least its requirement.
    # An employee with off-block starting at s works all days except s and s+1 (cyclic).
    # "The post office wants to meet its daily requirements"
    # assumption: cyclic_week_wrap (week is cyclic)
    def coverage_rule(m, day):
        idx = days.index(day)
        # Employees off on day are those whose off-block starts at day or day-1 (cyclic).
        off_start_today = days[idx]
        off_start_yesterday = days[(idx - 1) % n]
        return m.x[off_start_today] + m.x[off_start_yesterday] <= (
            sum(m.x[s] for s in m.S) - req[day]
        )

    # Rewrite coverage as a linear >= constraint without referencing total on RHS:
    # total - (x[day] + x[day-1]) >= req[day]
    # => sum_{s not in {day, day-1}} x[s] >= req[day]
    def coverage_rule2(m, day):
        idx = days.index(day)
        off_start_today = days[idx]
        off_start_yesterday = days[(idx - 1) % n]
        working = sum(
            m.x[s] for s in m.S if s != off_start_today and s != off_start_yesterday
        )
        return working >= req[day]

    model.coverage = pyo.Constraint(model.S, rule=coverage_rule2)

    return model

DATA = {
    "days": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"],
    # "Monday requires 17 employees,Tuesday requires13, Wednesday requires 15,

        "Mon": 17,
        "Tue": 13,
        "Wed": 15,
        "Thu": 19,
        "Fri": 14,
        "Sat": 16,
        "Sun": 11,
    },
    # "each full-time employee must work five consecutive days and then receive two days off"
    "work_days": 5,
    "off_days": 2,
    "week_length": 7,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    days = d["days"]
    n = d["week_length"]
    work = d["work_days"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Set of days of the week (Mon..Sun).
    model.DAYS = pyo.Set(initialize=days)

    # x[s] = number of employees whose 5-day block starts on day s.
    # assumption: shift_pattern_orientation -- x[s] covers s, s+1, ..., s+4 (cyclic).
    # "each full-time employee must work five consecutive days and then receive two days off"
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.DAYS, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimize total employees hired = sum of all shift-start variables.
    # "minimize the number of full-time employees who must be hired"
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[s] for s in m.DAYS)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Coverage: for each day t, sum of x[s] over shifts s whose 5-day block covers t
    # must be >= requirement[t]. Week is cyclic.
    # "The post office wants to meet its daily requirements"
    def coverage_rule(m, t):
        idx_t = days.index(t)
        # shifts starting at s cover t if t is within s, s+1, ..., s+4 (mod 7)
        covering = [
            s for s in days
            if (days.index(s) <= idx_t < days.index(s) + work)
            or (days.index(s) + work > n and idx_t < (days.index(s) + work) % n)
        ]
        return sum(m.x[s] for s in covering) >= d["requirement"][t]

    model.coverage = pyo.Constraint(model.DAYS, rule=coverage_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# All numeric constants from the problem statement.
DATA = {
    "days": ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"],
    # "Monday requires 17 employees,Tuesday requires13, Wednesday requires 15,
    #  Thursday requires 19, Friday requires 14, Saturday requires 16, Sunday requires 11."
    "requirement": {
        "Mon": 17,
        "Tue": 13,
        "Wed": 15,
        "Thu": 19,
        "Fri": 14,
        "Sat": 16,
        "Sun": 11,
    },
    # "each full-time employee must work five consecutive days and then receive two days off"
    "work_days": 5,
    "off_days": 2,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    days = d["days"]
    req = d["requirement"]
    n = len(days)

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # Set of days of the week (Mon..Sun in stated order).
    model.D = pyo.Set(initialize=days, ordered=True)

    # x[s] = number of employees whose 2-day off block starts on day s.
    # assumption: shift_pattern_orientation -- x[s] covers all days except s, s+1
    # "minimize the number of full-time employees who must be hired"
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.D, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: minimize total employees hired = sum of all shift-start variables.
    # "The post office wants to meet its daily requirements using only fulltime employees."
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[s] for s in m.D)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Coverage: each day must have at least its requirement covered.
    # An employee with off-block starting at s works every day except s and s+1
    # (cyclic week wrap). So day t is covered by all shifts s such that
    # t is not in {s, s+1} (mod 7).
    # "The post office wants to meet its daily requirements"
    def cover_rule(m, t):
        idx = days.index(t)
        off_start = (idx - 1) % n  # shift whose off block starts the day before t
        off_start2 = idx % n       # shift whose off block starts on t
        # Employees working on day t = all shifts except those off on t.
        return sum(m.x[s] for s in m.D if s != days[off_start] and s != days[off_start2]) >= req[t]

    model.cover = pyo.Constraint(model.D, rule=cover_rule)

    return model
